Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-08-07 | AMZN | Underweight | -4.3% | -4.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN at $274.48 — reduce, do not exit and do not short. Trim 40–45% of any existing AMZN exposure now, targeting a residual of roughly 2.0–2.5% of portfolio against a standard 5% single-name weight (i.e., 0.40–0.50x standard), and take a further 10–15% into the 282.00–287.20 shelf unless a daily close above 287.20 prints on >50M shares. Initiate no new position at $274.48. The structural invalidation for the residual is a daily close below 262.01 (the 7/31 gap low), not 270.73 — which is only ~0.4 ATR and would sell the core into routine post-gap noise; size the residual so a 1.5x ATR move (~$14, ~5.1% of price) fits the per-trade risk budget, which means materially smaller than pre-gap size. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on capex guidance, Q3 FCF/debt, and any private-AI mark reset.

**Investment Thesis**: **Direction.** The bear side wins on the two things that actually drive the multiple, and neither was answered at the table.

*Valuation is being paid on a synthetic earnings base.* Q2 GAAP EPS of $5.75 included a $50.49B upward revaluation on private securities; core EPS was roughly $1.86–$2.00, or about $8 annualized — and this is conceded by the aggressive analyst himself, who calls 274.48 "about 34x core." Paying a premium core multiple for a company with TTM FCF of –$11.63B and capex of $173.03B is a poor setup. The aggressive reframes the $122.3B private-AI book as "an embedded venture NAV at 11% of total assets," but the conservative's characterization is the correct one: it is a Level-3 mark tied to the same AI narrative that supports the multiple, so it is correlated beta, not free optionality. A funding-round reset produces a mechanical GAAP miss with no operating deterioration — the aggressive admits this — and that is precisely the event you want dry powder for rather than a full-sized core.

*The cash engine has turned and the margin levers are finite.* H1 FCF is –$26.99B; long-term debt went $68.8B → $133.0B (+93%) in six months; interest expense is +154.7% y/y to $1.31B a quarter; D&A is +42% against revenue +19.6%; gross margin expanded only ~50bp against a ~+150bp hurdle to hold operating margin flat from 2027; and the effective tax rate rose sharply (the analysts cite 600bp and 970bp respectively — the precise figure is unresolved, the direction is not). The aggressive's net-cash defense (~$29.7B pre-lease, $176.1B of cash and AFS securities, 20.9x interest coverage) proves solvency, which nobody contested, and never engages the direction of travel. That is why this is a trim, not a short — and also why the trim is warranted.

*The $650B obligation book is not demand visibility.* Contract liabilities are flat at ~$24.88B while the $650.03B is overwhelmingly purchase commitments, with $78.08B due inside twelve months. This is a forward-leverage/input-commitment signal running against, not for, the free-cash-flow thesis.

**Tape.** Lower highs since 8/03 (284.02 → 278.31), MACD histogram contracting three to four consecutive prints (4.62 → 4.09), volume 33.86M at 0.68x the 50.06M twenty-day average, price +16.0% above the 200SMA (236.54) and +10.9% above the 50SMA (247.51), and the 8/03 high of 287.20 stacked on the upper Bollinger at 287.33. The neutral is right that low volume on a tight range is ambiguous rather than proven distribution, and the conservative is right that the 50SMA inflection is largely a mechanical artifact of rolling off the July prints. Both readings point the same way for sizing: the marginal buyer has not shown up after a 26.7% three-session advance, so this is not a level to add at — which is exactly what the aggressive's own discipline concedes (buy 263–266 or add only above 287.20 on >50M volume).

**Why Underweight and not Sell.** All three seats converge on reducing, and none of them wants a flat book or an outright short, and they are right. Revenue +19.6% to $200.6B, operating income +43.2% to $27.46B on a 13.7% margin, G&A –6% and SBC –7.6% against 19.6% revenue growth, $176.1B of liquidity and 20.9x coverage. The prior 2026-07-31 AMZN decision credited the D&A-plus-margin-expansion datapoint as the bull's decisive evidence; on the current numbers that offset is eroding — D&A +42% with gross margin up only ~50bp — which strengthens the bear's forward-margin case but does not convert a high-quality franchise into a short. The aggressive's squeeze warning is also live: a daily close above 287.20 on >50M does not confirm the cap, it invalidates it, and this name gapped +15.3% three sessions ago. Express the view through underweight and trimming, not through a directional short or a zeroed position.

**Why 40–45% now and not the conservative's 50–60% to a 1.5–2.0% residual, and not the neutral's softer read.** I adopt the neutral's calibration with the conservative's risk discipline layered on. The conservative's 50–60% cut to 1.5–2.0% treats distribution as confirmed when the volume evidence is explicitly ambiguous, and his 270.73 trigger is 0.4 ATR from spot — the exact error recorded in the 2026-07-24 AMZN review, where caution expressed inside one ATR behaved like a directional short into a two-sided catalyst. The neutral's 2.0–2.5% target with 287.20/50M as the reassessment gate is sounder. I do, however, front-load toward the conservative end of the neutral's band (40–45%, not the low end) because the valuation/FCF/debt evidence is load-bearing in a way the tape is not, and because the 2026-07-22 lesson showed a light trim underperforms when the fundamental divergence is this wide. Critically, the event is now behind us rather than ahead, which removes the 07-24/07-28/07-29/07-30 failure mode of trimming hard into a binary print — the 15.3% gap is the market's verdict, and it has been delivered.

**What would change the call.** Upgrade toward Hold/market weight on a daily close above 287.20 with volume >50M (not on the level touch), or on a pullback into 263–266 that stabilizes with a close back above 265–270.73 on >50M volume and no credit or mark deterioration. Downgrade toward flat on a daily close below 262.01 on expanding volume, with 256.04/256.93, then 251.59, then 247.51 as the next references, and reduce a further 10% (not a panic exit) on a close below 270.73 on >50M shares as an early tell. Restore exposure only on evidence of contract liabilities beginning to reflect customer prepayments rather than purchase obligations, capex guidance at or below the current run-rate with FCF moving toward breakeven, long-term debt flat or declining, gross margin holding into the D&A step-up, or AWS segment disclosure showing continued acceleration.

**Explicit data gaps I am not underwriting to either side:** the news record has a 7/31–8/05 coverage gap and contains no article substantiating the earnings-beat details; no AWS segment revenue or operating income appears anywhere in the materials; no organic-versus-acquired revenue split; no Q3 capex or revenue guidance; no disclosed mark-to-model assumptions behind the $122.3B asset; no portfolio or holdings context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 258.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of –4.7% (raw –4.3%) confirms the Underweight direction was right, but five days is far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis built on FCF, leverage, and Level-3 marks — the call's substance remains unresolved. What the window does support is the sizing logic: trimming rather than shorting captured the downside without being whipsawed, though the –4.3% move brought price within roughly 0.7% of the 262.01 invalidation, meaning a stop placed ~1.5 ATR away can be tested in days on a post-gap name. The part it undercuts is the residual-position assumption — a 2.0–2.5% hold still bled in a week that vindicated the negative view. Lesson for next time: when the fundamental evidence is this one-sided, let the trim size (not the distance to a structural stop) carry the conviction, and pre-commit to re-scoring the invalidation level after any single-week move exceeding 1 ATR.

[2026-08-06 | AMZN | Overweight | -2.6% | -3.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AMZN, but do not buy at $272.26. The business case is decided for the bulls (Q2-2026 operating income +43.2% to $27.46B on a 13.69% margin, +226bps, with marketing +2.5%, G&A -6.0% and SBC -1.5% against +19.6% revenue); the entry case is decided for the bear, with only ~+4.3% to the $284.02 record against -3.8% to $262.01, -6.4% to VWMA $254.95, -9.1% to the 50-SMA and -11.9% to a full gap fill, with ATR at 3.52% of price. Build only on two earned triggers: (A) a tested $247-$262 confluence — require stabilization or a reclaim of $262.01 after the test, then deploy 0.20-0.25 of a standard unit, first bid no higher than ~$258, hard stop on a close below $245, with a deeper add at $250-$255 only on a wider close-stop below $242; (B) a close above $278.50 on >60M shares that holds two sessions for 0.25-0.30 unit, plus 0.15-0.20 unit on a subsequent close above $284.02 held two sessions. Cap the position at 0.75 unit until capex/revenue stops rising (25.8% in H1-2026 vs 17.7% in H1-2025), LTM FCF (-$11.6B) stops deteriorating, and one clean GAAP quarter prints after the $50.5B Q2 markup lap; only then allow 1.0 unit. If already at standard weight, hold and do not trim into a 76%-decayed-volume pullback; trim only the excess above 1.0 unit into $278-$284. Structural invalidation of the whole position: close below the 200-SMA at $236.25, or a full gap fill to $239.82 with no reclaim within five sessions. Horizon 3-6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not the contested question and should not be treated as one. The aggressive analyst won the argument that actually sets intrinsic value, and neither the conservative nor the neutral analyst contested the math: Q2-2026 operating income $27.46B, +43.2% y/y, operating margin 13.69% (+226bps), H1 margin 13.43% vs 11.62%, with marketing +2.5%, G&A -6.0% and SBC -1.5% against revenue +19.6%. Cost pools that large do not compress by accident; that is operating leverage, not mix. Even on the stripped-down number, H1-2026 core EPS of $3.63 vs ~$2.89 is +25.6%. LTM operating cash flow $161.4B, +33.2%, with core net income converting at 1.81x into cash, net cash ex-leases +$29.6B, interest coverage 20.9x, and a -64 day cash conversion cycle also mean the conservative's case is a monitoring item, not a solvency case. My own recent record on AMZN reinforces this: five consecutive Underweight calls into 2026-07/08 delivered +15.6%, +20.3%, +17.0%, +20.2% and +22.7% raw against the call, and each reflection reached the same conclusion — a bearish tape read inside a rising long-term trend carried no near-term directional information into the catalyst. I am not repeating that error.

The conservative and neutral analysts won two points that change sizing, not direction, and I carry both. First, earnings quality is not a footnote: $53.4B of non-operating fair-value marks were roughly 66% of pre-tax income, reported EPS $5.75 versus core ~$1.95, against a $122.3B non-marketable equity book (~20% of assets) that can reverse through the P&L; Q3 laps the $50.5B markup and the GAAP comparison will be mechanically ugly. Both are right that the aggressive analyst's "free option" framing is too generous — if the market re-rated AMZN on operating income, AMZN should be required to hold value on operating income, not be underwritten on marks. Second, the entry logic: a bid at $258 sits below the $262.01 level that structurally invalidates the 07-31 gap, so that tranche is a partial-gap-fill mean-reversion probe, not a continuation entry, and with a $245 stop only ~1.36 ATR away in a 3.52% ATR tape and a ~9.7% two-session gap precedent from February 2026, the plan's 0.40 unit is too large for a level below the invalidation line. The neutral analyst's ATR critique of the conservative probe is also correct and I am correcting for it: a $250-$255 bid held to the same $245 stop is less than one ATR of room, so the deeper add needs a wider close-stop below $242, or it does not happen.

The tape supports a constructive bias but not a purchase at spot — and here the trader is right and both the aggressive and conservative analysts are wrong. The bullish structure is genuine: the 07-31 gap of +15.32% on 129M shares, record $284.02, full stack aligned (272.26 > 10-EMA 260.87 > VWMA 254.95 > 50-SMA 247.45 > 200-SMA 236.25), 15.24% above a rising 200-SMA, 50-SMA inflecting 246.38 -> 247.45, VWMA climbing every session since the gap, and 129M -> 30.7M volume decay on a mere 4.14% give-back (profit-taking into a vacuum, not distribution). But it is unconfirmed: price closed back inside the $274.99/$278.56 six-month ceiling, RSI cooled 72.2 -> 63.2, the MACD histogram crested 4.62 -> 4.36, MFI 47.2 is not confirming, ATR expanded 39% to 3.52% of price and Bollinger width is 27.3% vs 12.9% a week earlier. The tell is that the aggressive analyst's own plan contains no purchase at spot — and that is decisive for execution.

Where the bear overreached and I reject it: the $650.0B "contractual obligations" figure is a liability note — purchase commitments, leases, capacity contracts — not a customer backlog; the aggressive analyst's demand-certainty framing is discounted, though $78.1B due within twelve months is still a real forward spending signal. "37.5x annualized core EPS" is crude (H1 core EPS roughly doubled, seasonality ignored) though directionally fair — there is no valuation cushion. And a tactical short into a stock 15.24% above a rising 200-SMA with VWMA climbing daily is a low-probability trade the conservative analyst himself hedged. The debt trend is genuinely wrong-way — gross LT debt $68.8B -> $133.0B, interest expense +155%, current ratio 1.033, receivables +30.1% against revenue +19.6% with allowance coverage thinning 3.54% -> 3.18%, D&A +44% while capex/revenue rises — but that is a cap on size, not a reason to be net negative.

Hence Overweight rather than Buy, and a cap of 0.75 unit rather than 1.0: the accumulation must be earned by price or by confirmation. Pre-plan the Q3 event: a sell-off on the ugly GAAP lapping headline while operating income growth and the ~13.7% margin hold, with price in the $247-$262 zone, is an add trigger per Trigger A rather than an exit; a sell-off accompanied by operating margin compression or capex/revenue moving higher means cut to the core and re-underwrite. Tripwires that force a re-rating to Underweight: (a) $650B of obligations failing to convert into visible capacity revenue while D&A runs +44%; (b) gross LT debt above ~$133B with interest expense still compounding at this rate and cash continuing to fall; (c) receivables outgrowing revenue with allowance coverage continuing toward and below 3.18%; (d) a close below $262.01 followed by a gap fill to $239.82 with no reclaim; (e) disclosure that the ~$350M Bezos sale is part of a materially larger 10b5-1 program; (f) any evidence that the $122.3B mark-to-model asset is reversing rather than being realized.

What I could not resolve from this packet and am not underwriting: there is no AWS segment revenue or operating income disclosure, no consensus estimates or peer comps to sanity-check ~37.5x core EPS, no options chain (so the $245/$262.01 close-stops are the hedge — express protection through size, not resting stops, given a documented -9% gap history), the news sample covers only the evening of 2026-08-05, and the "core EPS ~$1.95 / $3.63" figures are report-derived estimates rather than disclosed numbers. Any of those, if obtained, could move the sizing.

**Price Target**: 290.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -3.8% (raw -2.6%) went against the Overweight stance, though five sessions is far too short to test a 3-6 month thesis built on a $290 target and a Q3 operating-margin print. What the window does support is the entry discipline — refusing to buy at $272.26 was correct, and price is now moving toward the $262.01 invalidation line and the $247-$262 Trigger A zone — while undercutting the decision to carry Overweight rather than Neutral when the tape was already unconfirmed (RSI cooling, MACD cresting, ATR expanded 39%, price back inside the $274.99/$278.56 ceiling). The lesson: when the analysis concludes "do not buy at spot" and every execution trigger sits 4-12% lower, the rating should be Neutral with a buy-bias, not Overweight — a constructive rating without a position is a directional bet the entry plan itself contradicts.

**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AMZN at roughly standard weight (~0.85–1.0x of a standard allocation) rather than the 0.50–0.65x the plan proposes. Do not add at 272.65 — price is +5.54% above the 10 EMA (258.34) with ATR 9.98 (3.66%/day, +44.9% in five sessions) and the 07-31/08-03 breakout unconfirmed below 274.99/278.56 — but do not cut the core either: trim only any excess above standard weight into 278.56–281.41, and add in stages only on a decisive close above 281.41 on >70M shares with ATR below ~8.
